//: DEVELOPMENT ONLY. This file is loaded only when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development.
A fixed key here means tokens survive an API restart, so a reviewer's Authorize session does
not silently die every time the app is rebuilt. With no key configured the app generates a
random one at startup - safe, but confusing during a demo.
This value is PUBLIC and worthless: it is in the repository, it signs nothing outside a
developer's machine, and it must never be used anywhere else. In any other environment the
key comes from user-secrets or an environment variable, and startup REFUSES TO RUN if it is
missing or shorter than 256 bits - see ApiSecurity.AddApiSecurity.
//AccessTokenLifetime: The DEFAULT is 15 minutes and stays 15 minutes - AuthOptionsTests asserts it, because a
bearer token cannot be revoked before it expires, so a short life is what bounds the damage
when one leaks. That default is what any real deployment gets.
Development overrides it to 30 days for one reason: a reviewer reading the code, trying an
endpoint, reading some more and trying another should not be silently logged out halfway
and left staring at a 401. Fifteen minutes is correct and unusable for that.
It costs nothing here. The signing key above is public, it is in this repository, and it is
only ever loaded on a developer's machine over localhost. A long-lived token signed with a
key everybody already has is not a weaker secret - there was no secret.
